doc.title: Joe Muranyi interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2007

title: Defining jazz: jazz is what Louis Armstrong plays
summary: He struggles to define jazz and concludes it is the music Armstrong plays, before an audio clip of a session is played.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Well I’m curious, how do you explain to someone who is only familiar with jazz in the big sense, well what’s traditional jazz as opposed to modern jazz?

Okay Monk, you hit the nail — I’ve been working for years, I’ve got about 30 chapters in the computers about Louis Armstrong. And it’s very rarely discussed. It’s a very big problem of the music and it doesn’t get discussed much — what is jazz? And it’s a very difficult subject, and how do you define what is jazz. And I’ve tried, well it’s swing. Well no, a lot of music swings. It’s got soul, whatever. A lot of music has got soul. It’s got to have — I think it’s got to be a strong touch of the blues, some of the bended notes. It can’t be, I think Buddy DeFranco for instance has warmed up a lot. About ten years ago I heard somebody say hey, that’s really — I hear he is sort of phenomenal you know. But I didn’t get much warmth out of him. This is kind of nice. I said, “really?” I was so pleased. Number one I was pleased that I liked it you know? Because I’m very tough. People ask me do you like — well something about jazz — what do you like? Do you like jazz? And I say no I don’t like jazz, which is more true than the other that I like jazz. © Fillius Jazz Archive -20-

Because most stuff that passes for jazz today I do not care for. I don’t like it. And they’ve got a perfect right, they’ve got a right to play them blues but it doesn’t interest me. Okay. So it boils down to what is jazz? It’s got to have some blue notes, it’s got to swing, it’s got to be — it helps if it’s original. It’s sort of life generally it’s got to be in a certain bag, you know what I mean? A certain form, bebop or whatever, however. But it’s very hard to define. And I thought about it and thought about it and thought about it and for me jazz is the music that Louis Armstrong plays. It’s very simple, you can understand, you know when I say that you know what I’m talking about don’t you?
I do until, but Louis Armstrong played a lot of music sort of after the 20s and 30s also that may not have been really jazz. He jazzed it up.

Well his music, jazzing it up, what is jazz? Jazz is a feeling. You can play the straight — now Louis Armstrong, you know, he was the same man when he died as he was when he was young you know. That flame in him never died. And he could play the straight melody and melt your heart and that’s jazz. You could tell the difference between somebody very square and somebody swinging you know.
Yeah. I have a brief piece here of —
Remember that session? I mean I’m amazed at how many records are out there.
That was made on 57th Street here.
With, the guy that did Commodore Records, the A&R guy, can’t think of his name.
No it wasn’t Grauer. He’s famous. He was A&R Decca. He recorded Billie Holiday and everything.
He had Commodore Music up on 42nd Street and the Commodore Label.
Oh yeah. This is like Billy Crystal’s uncle.
